new_forms.what: the gap in his picture (tg:29) is the VALLEY BETWEEN TWO HUMPS of yesterday's profile (bimodal day), not its thin tails: on bimodal days does next-day POC / value land in the valley, vs the same-width band elsewhere in the range and vs unimodal days; trade = enter at the valley edge, out at the far edge

the green 'all groups' bar he boxes (tg:207, 216) is thin and fast: 18M volume (the smallest of the run), delta +14M = 78% of volume, 24.98 buys/s and 137 sell trades where its neighbours have 1-5 buys/s and 1,000-12,000 sells. Score = delta share x speed with few opposing trades -> continuation (dose); the red bar that ended it (60M, -16%, 4.6/s) is ordinary: so test entry on the thin fast bar, exit on first all-red

mousetrap as narrated (tg:170): FIRST test of the level gets few prints, SECOND test gets many times more volume with small-trade selling and no progress -> close back above; ratio of second to first test volume as dose

his other target (tg:227 picture): bid the old range high (B), offer the low of the small consolidation made right after the breakout (A), not one average candle; the retest came > 40 min later and after a +9 point run: order must rest until then

trend lasts until bars overlap (wa 18.10.19(1), R18): ride an impulse whose bars do not overlap (1h/4h), exit on the first bar that overlaps half of the leg; efficiency ratio as dose, vs fixed holding

his capitulation examples (wa 18.10.55(1), 56, 57) are not just 'all negative': every bucket is −3..−21% of its volume on a day that fell 2.6k-5.6k points; size of the negative share and of the fall as a 2-way dose (the sign-only version is R1); first check what is2_tsize already did
